## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Clean potency mapping and multi-axis phenotype: low-dose EC50 behavior, dose-log axis morphology, and taxel/Cyclopamine/demecarium reference contrasts are free of contradictions. Probability 0.82 is calibrated.

## Unblinding

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **Aurora kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **Aurora kinase inhibitors**.

## Reflection

The Aurora kinase inhibitor call was driven by an extreme and saturated large-nucleus polyploidy signal: frac_large_nucleus z=+24 to +32 and nuc_area/cell_area z~+17 to +32 from 0.03 uM (e8) through 30 uM (e2), with microscopist visual support (e4) and 6/10 Aurora neighbors in the reference atlas (e5). Integrated DNA increase (e11) favored true polyploidy over cell spreading, while intact tubulin argued against microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer or Eg5 alternatives.

Dose-response was the weakest part of the run: frac_large_nucleus, nuc_dna_integrated and multinucleate proxy all showed Spearman rho=-0.80 p=0.2 and cell_count rho=+0.40 p=0.6 (e9-e12) over only 4 wells. This flat/negative trend could have been misread as lack of dose dependence, but it reflected early saturation already at the lowest sampled dose of 0.03 uM with low cell numbers (111 cells in e8), so EC50 was never bracketed from below and p-values were non-informative.

Confidence at 0.82 was calibrated and correct: the minority atlas votes for DNA replication and DNA damage (2/10 each in e5) were appropriately retained at 0.07 each rather than dismissed, since polyploidy/endoreduplication alone cannot exclude those MoAs without phospho-markers, and compound lookup (e15) gave no structure for internal code AZ-A for orthogonal chemical confirmation.

What was right:
- Prioritized extreme frac_large_nucleus z=+25 to +32 across e2, e3, e7, e8 with concordant cell_area and nuc_area enlargement as polyploidy signal
- Used reference atlas 6/10 Aurora kinase inhibitors (e5) plus microscopist Aurora candidates (e4) to favor Aurora over DNA damage/replication
- Interpreted flat dose-response (e9-e12) as early saturation/potency rather than inactivity, and used lack of cell-count loss (e10) to favor cytostatic polyploidy over cytotoxic DNA damage

What was wrong or missed:
- Sampled only down to 0.03 uM which was already maximal, so true onset/EC50 was missed and dose-response rhos were non-significant p=0.2-0.6
- Relied on frac_multinucleate_proxy and nuc_dna_integrated without direct phospho-Aurora, phospho-H3, or gammaH2AX to mechanistically exclude DNA damage/replication retained at 0.07
- Did not quantitatively test tubulin or mitotic index to formally exclude Eg5/microtubule MoAs beyond qualitative intact-tubulin rationale

Proposed next experiment: DNA-content flow cytometry for >4N polyploidy plus immunofluorescence for phospho-Aurora A/B, phospho-histone H3 Ser10, alpha-tubulin midbody/central spindle morphology, and gammaH2AX to confirm Aurora inhibition with failed cytokinesis and exclude DNA damage.

## Citations

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [20484572](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20484572/): Aurora-C kinase deficiency causes cytokinesis failure in meiosis I and production of large polyploid oocytes in mice. *Mol Biol Cell* (2010) — Aurora-C deficiency causes cytokinesis failure and production of large polyploid cells, directly supporting large-nucleus polyploidy as an Aurora-inhibition phenotype.
- PMID [39639371](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39639371/): TNK2 Inhibitor (R)-9bMS Causes Polyploidization Through Mitotic Failure by Targeting Aurora B. *Cell Biochem Funct* (2024) — Targeting Aurora B causes polyploidization through mitotic failure.
- PMID [11266459](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11266459/): Drosophila aurora B kinase is required for histone H3 phosphorylation and condensin recruitment during chromosome condensation and to organize the central spindle during cytokinesis. *J Cell Biol* (2001) — Aurora B is required for histone H3 phosphorylation and organization of the central spindle during cytokinesis.
